name: pulse-dual-sculk-filter-L10

caption: One 10-tick pulse every time the input turns on and every time it turns off, for inputs held at least 1 second (20 ticks), and footsteps or dropped items nearby never set it off: the input makes a note block play when it turns on, and a torch on the input block opens a trapdoor when it turns off; a calibrated sculk sensor (a sound sensor), tuned by a comparator reading a chest to that one kind of sound, hears both and switches on for 10 ticks. metrics: L 30 gt, delay 6 gt, min-pulse 40 gt
caption: One pulse of 30, 46, 62... ticks every time the input turns on and every time it turns off, for inputs held at least 2 seconds (40 ticks): a copper bulb in the input cell shows each change of the input to an observer, which lights a copper bulb that a loop of repeaters resets; each extra row of repeaters adds 16 ticks. Detail: extendable family dual-edge-reset (n = 0): dual-edge with L = 30 + 16n gt, 33 + 4n blocks. Extension: lengthen the repeater U by one row: one more delay-4 repeater (on stone) in each column. Generator: mctas circuit pulse family dual-edge-reset --n N --out FILE.

name: d-latch-r7
metrics: latency 6 gt, enable high

name: dff-lock
metrics: latency 6 gt, edge rising, setup 1 gt, hold 1 gt
caption: D flip-flop, repeater-lock master-slave: the data runs through two repeaters A then B; each has a lock repeater beside it, and a repeater that is locked holds its output. The master lock reads the clock straight, so A follows d only while the clock is LOW; the slave lock reads the clock through a wall torch, so B passes only while the clock is HIGH. On the rising edge A freezes on d and B opens, so q takes d exactly at the edge.

name: shift2-lock
metrics: N 2, latency 6 gt, edge rising
caption: 2-bit shift register: two repeater-lock master-slave stages in series, the first stage output feeding the second stage data, both clocked from one dust line. Each stage is a pair of repeaters on the data line whose lock repeaters sit beside them: the master lock reads the clock straight (so it follows d while the clock is low) and the slave lock reads it through a wall torch (so it follows while the clock is high), which makes q take d one clock edge later, and two stages make it two.

caption: Shulker loader + unloader combo with a mode lever (track shulker-speed, clk-item). Lever off: a loader; lever on: an unloader, on the same chests. Core: clk-rt's always-on loader (dispenser D above the box cell X; observer Q on the pushed stone's cell re-fires D; comparator E + observer Q2 place the first box and restart after the supply ran out; sticky piston P's stone breaks the box and pushes the drop into the walled cell over the collection hopper K). Loader feed: chests a, b, c into one pool hopper over the feed hopper N. Unloader: hopper H under X empties it into chest d. The judge's 81-stack loader budget fills a, b, c in name order, so d stays empty in loader mode. One detector serves both modes. Comparator C reads X's level L into dust A, and K2 (compare, redstone block beside it) gives 15 only at L = 15. Z subtracts K2's signal (through repeater F, 8 gt) from A (through repeater R1, 2 gt), and repeater W squares it: S = (0 < L < 15). Because the full signal arrives 6 gt late, a box that is filled to 14 at once and topped up a gt later still makes S rise. V subtracts S (through repeater f) from S delayed (T2) and pulses for 4 gt when S falls: when a loading box gets full, or when an unloading box gets empty. P fires from V directly. (An earlier 85-block version also locked F from the lever; the in-game shrink, 85 -> 79 blocks, showed the combo badge passes without that lock and without two wall stones.) The lever's floor also powers a dust line under the build to the block holding the wall torch under H, so the torch (which locks H) goes off and H unloads only in unloader mode.

caption: Fastest always-on shulker loader, 7.4 items/s real fill rate (cycle 4681 gt per box of 1728 cobblestone: the ceiling of hoppers under 3 item chests; 3x the hopper loader; track shulker-speed, clk-item). The dispenser D above the box cell X places empty boxes; a sticky piston P breaks a full box and its stone pushes the drop into the cell over the collection hopper K. Items: chests a and b feed a pool hopper H1 (a from above, b through a side hopper); hopper N under H1 pulls from it and feeds X from the south; chest c feeds N directly through its south side, and hopper U under N pulls from N into the dropper Y under X (facing up); H1's push runs west and down a hopper chain into Y's west face. So N, which gives every new box its first item, never starves while any chest has items, and Y gets 5 items/s. Gate: comparator C reads X's level L through a stone into dust A; K2 (compare, redstone block beside it) passes only a full box, to the piston through two delay-4 repeaters and onto the side of subtract comparator Z, so Z passes L only while 0 < L < 15; repeater W squares it into the rear of G, a subtract comparator looping through repeater R into its own side (an 8 gt clock while the gate is open). Two observers fire Y: Q under Y watches G (it catches G's on-change; the off-change comes while Q is still on) and a second observer under the stone north of Y watches a delay-2 repeater on G's output, which changes 4 gt later; together they give Y a rising edge every 4 gt, 5 items/s. Y never fires at an empty cell, a breaking box or air (a dropper facing a full box keeps its item). Always-on: comparator E reads D and observer Q2 fires D when D's contents go between empty and not; the dispenser is powered through a stone so Y is not QC-fired by it. Shrunk in the game from 108 blocks (with `--min-rate`): two drop-cell walls and an unused delay line from Q2 into the gate are not needed.

caption: Fast always-on shulker loader with restart AND flush, 7.4 items/s (track shulker-speed, clk-item). It is shulker-speed-loader-dropper75 plus two additions. (1) A placement one-shot. Comparator A on the dispenser outputs into a dust line, and an observer at its far end fires whenever the dispenser level changes (a box placed or arriving). The dot dust on top of the collection hopper then points into the box cell and powers the closed box, which is a conductor, so the bottom dropper fires once by quasi-connectivity. name: shulker-unloader-1wide
metrics: boxes/min 0.087, items/s 2.50, first box 13859 gt, cycle 13838 gt, hoppers awake 3, badges always-on+16-stack+unstackable+colours+box-starved+drop-free+tileable(1), bill 16 iron, 8 quartz, 26 redstone, 1 slime
caption: A one-block-wide unloader you can line up side by side with no gap: a dispenser drops each full box onto a hopper that empties it, and when the box is empty a piston breaks it into a second hopper that sends it on.  How it works (no redstone dust and no comparator side inputs, so neighbouring copies never touch each other's signals): - A comparator reads the emptying hopper. That hopper holds exactly 1 item while the box still has items, because it pushes and then pulls in the same tick. - When the hopper empties, the torch on the block the comparator powers (through a repeater) lights 3 gt later, and the sticky piston pushes a stone into the box cell. That is soon enough that the emptying hopper is still on its cooldown and cannot grab the box. The box's drop is pushed into the cell above the output hopper, which catches it at once. - An observer under the comparator toggles a copper bulb on every change of the comparator, so the bulb is lit while the box has items. While it is unlit, a torch under the block keeps the block powered, which ends the piston's pulse and holds it off until the next box's first item. Every comparator starts at 0, so the design is consistent as placed in any rotation. - An observer over the piston, watched by an observer on the dispenser, fires the dispenser after each break. A comparator reads the dispenser through a stone, and two observers watch it. When the dispenser gets its first box, they power the boxes hopper above it, which fires the dispenser by quasi-connectivity. That covers the start and refills after the supply ran out.

name: shulker-loader-pitch3
metrics: boxes/min 0.087, items/s 2.50, first box 13867 gt, cycle 13840 gt, hoppers awake 4, badges always-on+16-stack+unstackable+colours+restart+top-up+box-starved+drop-free+tileable(3), bill 21 iron, 6 quartz, 35 redstone, 1 slime
caption: A shulker box loader you can line up side by side every 3 blocks: a hopper fills the box from above, a comparator watches it, and when it is full a piston breaks it into a hopper that sends it on, while a dispenser underneath places the next empty box. Details: 1 wide is impossible, because a box cell in a 1-block slice has only 4 free faces for 5 jobs (place, feed, read, break, drop) and every signal there is on/off, so "full" (15 against 14) cannot be read; 2 wide does not work either, because a signal cannot cross from one column to the other without also reaching the neighbouring copy. Here the feed hopper is above the box cell, the dispenser below it facing up, and the read on its east side: a comparator in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, 15 only when the box is full. That signal runs north along the third column through two repeaters and back west into the stone behind a sticky piston, whose stone breaks the box and pushes it into the drop cell over the output hopper. The dispenser fires whenever its contents change (a comparator reads it through a stone; two observers watch that comparator and power the stone under the dispenser), which places the first box and refills after a box shortage, and after every break (an observer under the first repeater of the full line, watched by an observer that powers the read-through stone).

caption: Sees everything that can happen to the target block on one output: placed, removed, changed, reshaped by its neighbors, or only updated (13 blocks, reacts in 1 tick). It is the fast piston BUD below plus an observer: the observer catches reshaping, which no piston can feel, and kicks the piston, so every event gives the same 5-tick pulse. Detail: a stone on the slime block cuts the step between two dusts; the piston, armed by quasi-connectivity (power that reaches it only through the block above it, so it has not noticed it yet), takes the stone off the step in the tick after a block update; the observer under the low dust watches the target below the piston and its pulse climbs into the low dust, lighting the output and updating the piston.

axis: detects place remove state update, latched (manual reset)
name: bud-latched-qc
metrics: detects place remove state update, latency 3 gt, reset manual, off 1 gt after it, re-arm 2 gt, footprint 5 cells, tileable every 2 (0 2 0)
caption: Turns on at the first block update next to the target and stays on until you reset it: the smallest latched BUD, 2 blocks. A sticky piston is powered without having noticed it (the power reaches it only through the block above its neighbor, called quasi-connectivity); the first update makes it notice and push a redstone block next to the output, where it stays. Detail: the reset input is the arming redstone block itself: taking it away updates the piston, it retracts and pulls the block back (the output goes off 1 tick later); putting it back arms it without an update. A change by shape alone sends no block update: not detected.

name: bud-qc-nojam
metrics: detects place remove state update, latency 3 gt, pulse 2 gt, re-arm 8 gt, footprint 5 cells, tileable every 3 (0 0 3)
caption: A classic BUD (it sees pure block updates, which no observer can) that never jams, even on two updates 2 ticks apart: 5 blocks. Two plain pistons pass a package back and forth: a slime block carrying the arming redstone block and an observer. Detail: piston P is armed by quasi-connectivity (power through the block above it that it has not noticed); an update makes it push the package east, the redstone block lands beside the output, the moved observer fires and updates piston Q, which pushes the package home and re-arms P without an update.
